classification.difficultyReason: Combine squared exact ratios and reciprocal ratios across several quadrants, retaining the signs of all three terms.

answer.short:
$\frac{3}{4}$

Use related angles and reciprocal ratios, then square the required ratios before combining the terms.
answer.worked:
Using related angles and quadrant signs,
$$\sin120^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2},\qquad \cos315^{\circ}=\frac{1}{\sqrt2},\qquad \tan225^{\circ}=1.$$
The reciprocal ratios are
$$\operatorname{cosec}270^{\circ}=\frac{1}{-1}=-1,\qquad \sec180^{\circ}=\frac{1}{-1}=-1,\qquad \cot315^{\circ}=\frac{1}{-1}=-1.$$
$$\begin{align*}\sin^{2}120^{\circ}\operatorname{cosec}270^{\circ}-\cos^{2}315^{\circ}\sec180^{\circ}-\tan^{2}225^{\circ}\cot315^{\circ}&=\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)^2(-1)-\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\right)^2(-1)-1^2(-1)\\\sin^{2}120^{\circ}\operatorname{cosec}270^{\circ}-\cos^{2}315^{\circ}\sec180^{\circ}-\tan^{2}225^{\circ}\cot315^{\circ}&=-\frac34+\frac12+1\\\sin^{2}120^{\circ}\operatorname{cosec}270^{\circ}-\cos^{2}315^{\circ}\sec180^{\circ}-\tan^{2}225^{\circ}\cot315^{\circ}&=\frac34.\end{align*}$$
